land.text: the pueblo of Sonoma and the country around it, then Mexican Alta California

predecessors.note: The Bear Flag party seized 'the undefended' Sonoma on 14 June 1846; the infobox: 'Independence from Mexico declared: June 14, 1846'.

land.text: the same area, occupied by the US military at Sonoma on 9 July 1846

successors.note: The infobox lists the United States and an 'Interim government of California' as successors; on 22 August 1846 Stockton reported that 'California is entirely free from Mexican dominion' (page).

capitals.name: Sonoma
capitals.note: Infobox 'Capital: None'; 'The Sonoma Barracks became the headquarters for the remaining twenty-four rebels'.

rulers.name: William B. Ide
rulers.title: leader of the Bear Flag party at Sonoma
rulers.note: The page does not call him president; the rebels 'elected him their leader' and his proclamation is dated 'Head Quarters Sonoma, June 15, 1846'.

correction.text: the Sonoma area only, and for 1846 only (14 June to 9 July): not the wider Bay Area shape, and not 1847

keyframe_review.note: 15,546 km2 (49 cells) for 1846-1847. The page and the Bear Flag Revolt page give no area, only 'an area north of San Francisco, in and around what is now Sonoma County' and 'a small area'. By the gazetteer the Cliopatria shape is centred on the Bay Area and reaches 36.3N (Monterey Bay) to 38.8N, i.e. it takes in San Francisco Bay, San Jose and Monterey Bay, which the page does not give to the rebels (Monterey was taken by the US Navy on 7 July, not by the Bears). The infobox gives 14 June to 9 July 1846, so 1847 is wrong. The correction is a 40 km circle on Sonoma (about 5,000 km2).

region.text: an area north of San Francisco, in and around what is now Sonoma County, around the Sonoma pueblo and its barracks

ledger.note: 14 June 1846: the Bear Flag party seizes Sonoma. 'Before dawn on Sunday, June 14, 1846, over 30 American insurgents arrived at the pueblo of Sonoma'; infobox 'Independence from Mexico declared: June 14, 1846'. The name 'California Republic' 'appeared only on the flag the insurgents raised in Sonoma'; Ide's proclamation is dated 15 June.

region.text: an area north of San Francisco, in and around what is now Sonoma County, around the Sonoma pueblo and its barracks

ledger.note: 9 July 1846: the Bear Flag Republic ends. The revolt 'ended when Navy Lieutenant Joseph Revere' raised the US flag at the Sonoma Barracks; infobox 'Occupation of Sonoma by the U.S. military: July 9, 1846'. On 5 July Frémont had proposed that the Bears unite with his party and the rebel force was 'subsumed into the California Battalion'; Monterey had fallen to the US Navy on 7 July.

wars.name: Bear Flag Revolt

zones.text: an area north of San Francisco, in and around what is now Sonoma County, around the Sonoma pueblo and its barracks

wars.outcome: A 25-day republic around Sonoma (14 June to 9 July 1846), ended when the US Navy raised the American flag at Sonoma Barracks; the area passed to the United States, whose war with Mexico is carried in the USA dossier.
wars.note: The USA dossier opens its own contest with Mexico on 14 June 1846; Frémont's California Battalion (5 July) merged the rebels into the US Army.

certainty.note: A rebel base around Sonoma, no surveyed line: the page says only 'a small area north of San Francisco'.

sources.title: California Republic
sources.note: Infobox dates 14 June to 9 July 1846, 'Capital: None', Sonoma as base, 'an area north of San Francisco, in and around what is now Sonoma County', Ide's proclamation 15 June, Revere at Sonoma 9 July.

sources.title: Bear Flag Revolt
sources.note: Sonoma, Napa Valley, Sutter's Fort, San Rafael; Frémont's California Battalion 5 July 1846; Monterey 7 July; 'a small area north of San Francisco was controlled by the Bear Flag rebels'.

notes:
Rebel republic of 25 days (14 June to 9 July 1846). Cliopatria's single shape (1846-1847, 15,546 km2, 49 cells) is too large in space (it covers the whole Bay Area down to Monterey Bay) and in time (the 1847 year is wrong); the correction is a 40 km circle around Sonoma and the year 1846 alone. Typed 'rebel' because the page says the 'California Republic' name 'appeared only on the flag' and never had a formal government (infobox 'Capital: None').

Pages opened (2 of 1-2): California Republic and Bear Flag Revolt. Not on them: the Treaty of Cahuenga (13 January 1847), the Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo and statehood; those belong to the USA dossier. Neither page gives an area.

Counterparts: federated-republic-of-mexico (am-08) and united-states-of-america (am-07-c; its ledger has the 14 June 1846 Bear Flag contest against Mexico).

Gazetteer: 'Sonoma' has no place entry (Santa Rosa, Vallejo and San Francisco do); the area is a lon/lat circle at 38.292N, 122.458W and Sonoma is listed for the gazetteer agent.
